target_customer: JavaScript and Node.js developers who want to prototype server-side code in the browser
problem: Trying a Node module or prototyping server-side JavaScript required local setup. RunKit (formerly Tonic) offered sandboxed browser notebooks with npm modules available without installing them.
business_model: Developer tool, free with paid tiers; revenue not found

founders.name: Francisco Tolmasky
founders.background_notes: VentureBeat says he founded the company.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running arbitrary user code safely in sandboxes with on-demand npm module resolution and rich result visualization is demanding for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Sandbox infrastructure took work to replicate, but notebook-style REPLs were an obvious product category.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe acquired it in September 2016 and kept it as a separate subsidiary.

market_need_then: Tonic drew attention on Hacker News in August 2015 as a data visualizing REPL for Node.js (342 points), indicating developer interest.

identity.voice_and_tone: Described as a node playground in your browser

rebrands.why: not stated; VentureBeat reports the rename alongside the Stripe deal

branding.community_and_virality: Embeds in npm package pages and docs; a dev.to post and Hacker News launch discuss it.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely embedded in Node documentation, but the brand's drivers were not documented.

outcome_analysis: The product began as Tonic in 2015, joined YC in Summer 2016 and was acquired by Stripe on September 13, 2016, with terms and funding undisclosed, only weeks after the batch started. It was renamed RunKit and kept running independently under Stripe. The quick exit suggests the product and team were valued for developer tooling skills rather than revenue.
notes: runkit.com returned HTTP 503. No funding information found: VentureBeat says funding was not disclosed. The YC page lists three founders although team size is 2. The Hacker News item was surfaced in search results, not opened. Competitor search returned only current comparison pages, so the list is empty. The 2019 DevToolsDigest item surfaced in search repeats the acquisition news.
